title: Three Years in Melbourne
summary: Clara Aspinall reached Melbourne by steamship in March 1858 and stayed for three years with her brother, to whom the book is dedicated, leaving in May 1861. She describes the city and St Kilda: its streets and buildings, its society with its balls and picnics, Parliament and the Governor, the churches and charities, newspapers, the climate, house rents, servants, prices, and dress. In the winter of 1860 she travelled up-country by railway, coach, and horse to Carisbrook, Avoca, Castlemaine, Sandhurst, and Kyneton, and writes about the gold-field towns and the Chinese diggers. A long chapter gives advice on who should and should not emigrate, one chapter is written for children, and the last two describe the voyage home. Ships and some people are left unnamed.
